predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria draws Lorraine and Bar inside Holy Roman Empire Minor States until 1430 (all 75 cells)

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Lorraine and Bar, annexed on the death of Stanisław Leszczyński on 23 February 1766 and reorganized as a province

ledger.x: 1431: Duke Charles II dies and René of Anjou, husband of his daughter Isabella, inherits Lorraine and Bar.
1453: Bar parts from Lorraine in Cliopatria's shapes.
1473: René II succeeds his cousin as Duke of Lorraine.
1475: Charles the Bold of Burgundy occupies Lorraine and drives René II out of Nancy.
1480: Bar passes to René II and is united with Lorraine.
1482: René II conquers the prévôté of Virton and annexes it to Bar.
1661: the French withdraw and Charles IV returns.
1670: France occupies Lorraine again and Charles IV goes into exile.
1697: the Treaty of Ryswick returns Lorraine.
1702: France occupies parts of Lorraine again.
1737: Stanisław Leszczyński becomes Duke of Lorraine and Bar.
1766: Stanisław dies and France annexes Lorraine.

wars.name: War of the Lorraine Succession
wars.outcome: Antoine de Vaudémont won the Battle of Bulgnéville (2 July 1431) and René of Anjou was captured and handed to the Duke of Burgundy; Sigismund awarded Lorraine to René at Basel in 1434; the marriage of René's daughter Yolande to Antoine's son Frederick, 'only…

wars.name: Burgundian Wars (Lorraine campaign)
wars.outcome: René II recovered Nancy (5 October 1476) and 'defeated and killed Charles at the Battle of Nancy (5 January 1477)'.

wars.name: French occupation of Lorraine (1633-1661)
wars.outcome: France invaded in 1633, 'was able to occupy the duchy in 1634 and retained it until 1661 when Charles IV was restored'.

wars.name: French occupation of Lorraine (1670-1697), ended by the Treaty of Ryswick
wars.outcome: France invaded in 1670 and Charles IV went into exile; the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick returned the Duchy of Lorraine.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Lorraine)
wars.outcome: 'parts of Lorraine, including the capital Nancy, were again occupied by France'; the page does not date the withdrawal.

wars.name: Settlement of the War of the Polish Succession (Lorraine and Bar)
wars.outcome: Stanisław Leszczyński received the duchies of Lorraine and Bar for his lifetime, to pass to Louis XV's wife on his death; Francis Stephen was indemnified with Tuscany (Treaty of Vienna, signed 18 November 1738).

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened; the outlines are Cliopatria's.
